"BATMAN: SHADOWS OF GOTHAM – COMPLETE 3D GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT
Create a realistic, fully playable 3D open-world Batman action-adventure game called BATMAN: SHADOWS OF GOTHAM.
This must be an actual playable 3D game, not just a picture, slideshow, or collection of descriptions. Include playable characters, environments, animations, combat, missions, dialogue, cutscenes, vehicles, gadgets, collectibles, enemies, and boss battles.
1. GRAPHICS AND CHARACTER DESIGN
Use realistic, high-quality 3D graphics with:
Realistic human character models.
Natural body proportions and believable anatomy.
Detailed faces, hair, clothing, and animations.
Realistic lighting, shadows, reflections, and weather.
Detailed Gotham City buildings and streets.
Realistic movement and facial expressions.
Cinematic camera angles and transitions.
Characters must have their recognizable colors, costumes, and appearances. Do not randomly change their clothing or give them oversized accessories.
Batman – Bruce Wayne
Black and dark-gray armored Batsuit.
Black Batman cowl with pointed bat ears.
Black cape.
Batman symbol on his chest.
Utility belt.
Grapple gun.
Batarangs.
Smoke pellets.
Robin – Dick Grayson
Red superhero suit with black details.
Yellow accents.
Black boots and gloves.
No cowl, no helmet, and no oversized head accessories.
His face and hair must remain visible.
Robin symbol on his chest.
Robin Wings, a grapple gun, and a Bo staff.
Red, yellow, and black motorcycle with an R symbol.
Alfred
Gray hair.
Black formal suit.
White shirt.
Black tie.
Older gentleman appearance.
No weapons, oversized accessories, or superhero costume.
Two-Face – Harvey Dent
Black hair.
White-and-black formal suit.
Recognizable Two-Face appearance.
No red suit.
No oversized sharp objects or exaggerated head accessories.
Include his signature coin.
His facial injury should be represented in a non-graphic but recognizable way.
Catwoman – Selina Kyle
Black fitted superhero suit.
Black cowl.
Small, slightly pointed cat ears.
The ears must not be excessively large or sharp.
Realistic human proportions.
Include her recognizable appearance and movement.
The Riddler
Yellow suit.
Black question marks covering the suit.
Green cane.
Recognizable Riddler appearance.
Green question-mark-themed equipment and puzzles.
Other villains
Give every villain their recognizable traditional colors, clothing, equipment, and appearances:
Joker: Purple suit, green hair, pale face.
Penguin: Formal dark clothing, recognizable umbrella.
Bane: Large, muscular appearance, recognizable mask.
Killer Croc: Reptilian appearance.
Poison Ivy: Green-themed clothing and plant abilities.
Mr. Freeze: Blue-and-white armored suit and ice equipment.
Mad Hatter: Recognizable hat and colorful clothing.
Red Hood: Red helmet and dark clothing.
Jason Todd: Recognizable appearance and costume.
Do not give every villain the same clothing, colors, face, or body model.
2. THE COMPLETE STORY
The game begins in 1982.
Bruce Wayne is a young boy leaving a movie theater with his parents, Thomas and Martha Wayne.
An older gunman confronts the family and demands money. Thomas gives him $200, but the gunman shoots both parents.
Show this as a serious, emotional, cinematic scene without graphic details. Bruce is left crying beside his parents.
The screen fades to black.
26 YEARS LATER – 2008
Bruce discovers documents and a billion-dollar inheritance in his father's old jacket pocket.
He uses the money to purchase a mansion and establish Wayne Enterprises.
He hosts parties and invites friends, including Harvey Dent.
One year later, Harvey suffers a terrible incident that changes his life and eventually turns him into Two-Face.
DISCOVERING THE CAVE
Bruce discovers an enormous abandoned cave and arrives carrying luggage.
An old man approaches him.
Alfred: \"Excuse me, sir. Are you looking for something in here? Because I'm pretty sure nothing is in this cave. And it's old, too, just as me.\"
Bruce: \"I'm trying to do something with this place. What makes you think that you can tell me what to do and what not to do?\"
Alfred: \"I understand you are trying to stand your ground. But you need to leave because you're trespassing.\"
Bruce refuses to leave. Alfred eventually walks away.
Bruce moves computers, equipment, and belongings into the cave.
Three months later, Alfred returns.
Alfred: \"Excuse me, sir. Remember me? I'm Alfred.\"
Bruce: \"What are you doing here?\"
Alfred: \"I'm trying to help you make this cave.\"
Bruce accepts his help.
BUILDING THE BATCAVE
Bruce and Alfred spend several months constructing:
Computer command center.
Batman suit machine.
Batmobile garage.
Underground elevator.
Detective workstation.
Gadget workshop.
Communications center.
Equipment storage.
Alfred helps build the Batmobile, prepare batarangs, smoke pellets, and grapple guns, and purchase a self-defense book.
BRUCE'S TRAINING
Bruce studies the book and trains extensively.
Include:
Punches.
Kicks.
Roundhouse kicks.
Grappling.
Defensive movements.
Dodging.
Counterattacks.
Push-ups.
Weight lifting.
Sit-ups.
Treadmill training.
Several months later, Bruce finally puts on the Batsuit.
ROBIN'S ARRIVAL
A bald teenager enters the Batcave.
Bruce: \"Who the hell are you, kid?\"
Dick: \"I'm Dick Robin Grayson, and I'm old enough to fight crime. I'm over 17!\"
Bruce asks Alfred to make him a Robin suit.
One month later, Alfred completes the costume and equipment.
Robin receives:
Red-and-black suit.
Robin Wings.
Grapple gun.
Bo staff.
Utility belt.
Red, yellow, and black motorcycle with an R symbol.
Robin also learns self-defense and trains before joining Batman.
3. OPEN-WORLD GOTHAM CITY
Create a large, explorable Gotham City.
Include:
Downtown.
Residential neighborhoods.
Industrial district.
Gotham Harbor.
Financial district.
Abandoned subway stations.
Underground sewers.
Gotham Police Department.
Wayne Enterprises.
Wayne Manor.
Rooftops.
Criminal warehouses.
Villain hideouts.
Citizens should walk, drive, talk, and react naturally.
Batman and Robin must be able to speak with citizens, investigate crimes, discover clues, and receive missions.
4. PLAYABLE BATMAN AND ROBIN
Allow the player to switch between Batman and Robin during gameplay.
Both characters must have their own:
Character models.
Animations.
Dialogue.
Gadgets.
Fighting styles.
Vehicles.
Abilities.
They must be able to fight together, assist each other, and perform coordinated actions.
Include:
Grappling between buildings.
Gliding from rooftops.
Jumping across buildings.
Climbing.
Vehicle driving.
Combat.
Stealth gameplay.
Batman and Robin must not have identical abilities.
5. COMBAT SYSTEM
Create a responsive third-person combat system.
Include:
Punching.
Kicking.
Roundhouse kicks.
Combos.
Counterattacks.
Dodging.
Blocking.
Grappling.
Stun animations.
Team attacks.
Stealth takedown animations.
Enemy reactions.
Make combat animations smooth and realistic.
Include an on-screen combo counter and health indicators.
Both Batman and Robin must be able to use their respective gadgets during combat.
Batman's equipment
Batarangs.
Grapple gun.
Smoke pellets.
Utility belt.
Detective equipment.
Robin's equipment
Robin Wings.
Grapple gun.
Bo staff.
Utility belt.
6. DETECTIVE MODE
Batman must have detective mode.
When activated:
Highlight important clues.
Identify suspicious objects.
Show footprints and evidence.
Highlight interactive objects.
Analyze crime scenes.
Display enemy positions.
Robin must NOT have detective mode.
Robin can still investigate ordinary objects and help Batman discover clues through dialogue.
7. CRIMINALS AND MOB MISSIONS
The first major part of the campaign must focus on ordinary criminals and organized crime.
Include:
Criminal gangs.
Mob organizations.
Warehouse investigations.
Street crimes.
Robberies.
Hostage-rescue missions.
Criminal hideouts.
Police conversations.
Witness interviews.
Give criminals different appearances, clothing, dialogue, and combat behaviors.
Criminals should have different levels of difficulty.
8. THE RIDDLER'S 50 CHALLENGES
Include 50 collectible challenges throughout Gotham.
They must include:
25 Riddler trophies.
15 hidden clues.
10 riddles.
Make the riddles challenging and interactive.
The Riddler must communicate with Batman and Robin through messages and recordings.
His trophies should be hidden throughout buildings, rooftops, tunnels, and secret rooms.
9. VILLAINS AND BOSS BATTLES
Include these villains:
Joker.
Penguin.
The Riddler.
Two-Face.
Bane.
Killer Croc.
Catwoman.
Poison Ivy.
Mr. Freeze.
Mad Hatter.
Jason Todd.
Red Hood.
Every villain must have:
A unique personality.
Recognizable appearance.
Dialogue and conversations.
Their own hideout.
Criminal associates or goons.
Individual missions.
Special abilities.
Unique boss encounters.
Difficulty system
Larger and more powerful villains should be difficult and capable of defeating Batman and Robin.
Intelligent villains should use puzzles, traps, strategies, and special abilities.
Ordinary criminals should be easier to defeat.
Boss encounters must feel different from ordinary fights.
10. CHARACTER CONVERSATIONS
Include conversations with:
Alfred.
Robin.
Catwoman.
Harvey Dent.
Two-Face.
Gotham citizens.
Police officers.
Criminals.
Mob members.
Villains.
Give characters natural voices, facial expressions, reactions, and dialogue.
Do not make characters stand silently while conversations happen.
11. VEHICLES
Include:
Batmobile.
Robin's motorcycle.
Allow players to drive both vehicles around Gotham.
Include realistic steering, acceleration, braking, vehicle sounds, headlights, and driving animations.
12. REALISTIC CUTSCENES
Create cinematic story scenes with:
Character facial expressions.
Natural dialogue animations.
Camera movement.
Realistic walking and running.
Characters looking at one another while speaking.
Environmental sound effects.
Weather effects.
Smooth transitions between gameplay and cutscenes.
The opening scene showing Bruce's parents dying must be included as a serious, emotional part of the origin story, without graphic imagery.
Do not skip important story scenes.
13. PLOT TWISTS
Include several major surprises involving:
Harvey Dent becoming Two-Face.
The Riddler's hidden organization.
Jason Todd's connection to Batman.
Red Hood's identity and motives.
The Joker's larger plan.
Make the twists unfold gradually through clues, missions, conversations, and cinematic scenes.
14. FINAL MISSION
The final campaign mission involves the Joker launching a major operation across Gotham.
Batman and Robin must:
Investigate the criminal activity.
Rescue citizens.
Stop the criminal organizations.
Find Joker's hideout.
Defeat his goons.
Confront the Joker in a final boss battle.
End with Batman and Robin standing together on a Gotham rooftop as the Bat-Signal appears.
15. POST-GAME VILLAIN MODE
After completing the entire campaign, unlock a special villain mode.
Allow players to replay the game and select villains as playable characters.
Include:
Joker.
Penguin.
Riddler.
Two-Face.
Bane.
Killer Croc.
Poison Ivy.
Mr. Freeze.
Mad Hatter.
Jason Todd.
Red Hood.
Give each playable villain unique animations, dialogue, abilities, and missions.
Also allow players to replay the original Batman and Robin campaign.
16. GAME LENGTH AND QUALITY
Target a main story lasting approximately 4–7 hours, depending on exploration and mission completion.
Include:
Multiple story chapters.
Side missions.
Boss battles.
Collectibles.
Open-world activities.
Character conversations.
Unlockable content.
Replayable missions.
17. IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS
Do not leave out requested characters, gadgets, story events, or gameplay features.
Do not substitute incorrect character designs.
Do not give Robin a cowl or detective mode.
Do not give Alfred a superhero costume.
Do not give Two-Face a red suit or oversized sharp accessories.
Do not give Catwoman oversized ears.
Do not give the Riddler an incorrect costume or cane.
Make the characters visually consistent throughout the entire game, including cutscenes and gameplay.
Prioritize a working, playable game over unnecessarily complicated features.
Implement the game in stages if necessary. Test each stage before building the next one.
Fix coding errors, broken controls, missing assets, and build failures before reporting completion.
FINAL GOAL: Create a complete, realistic, playable 3D Batman and Robin open-world game with a cinematic story, Gotham exploration, detective investigations, gadgets, combat, villains, boss battles, and post-game villains

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a playable 3D Batman and Robin action-adventure in the existing project, prioritizing working gameplay and testing over attempting every requested feature at full AAA scale.

## Requirements
- Title: **BATMAN: SHADOWS OF GOTHAM**; include Gotham exploration, playable Batman and Robin, combat, gadgets, detective mode exclusive to Batman, missions, collectibles, villains, boss fights, vehicles, story scenes, and a post-game villain mode.
- Preserve requested character designs and story details; Robin has no cowl or detective mode, Alfred is not a superhero, and villain appearances should be distinguishable.
- Build and test the game without asking clarifying questions; note reasonable assumptions on completion.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing Three.js browser game rather than replacing its framework.
- Scope the challenge count to 25 trophies, 15 clues, and 10 interactive riddles.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the browser title/branding and added HUD markup for combo count, detective mode, and interactive riddles.
- Improved character figure construction and added distinct visual details for Batman, Robin, Alfred, Harvey, Selina, and several villains.
- Added villain dialogue data and expanded the villain roster with Jason Todd.
- Expanded collectibles from 40 to 50, categorized as trophies and clues; added 10 riddle objects and answer interactions.

### Active
- Integrate the new gameplay systems with existing objectives, interaction hints, collectibles, controls, and story progression.
- Test the browser build, repair any runtime or syntax errors, and capture/inspect a screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` around recent edits; fix syntax/runtime issues and check references such as villain names, collectibles, riddle interactions, and character switching.
2. Implement remaining controls and gameplay: detective mode (Batman only), combo HUD, improved vehicle/gadget behavior, and mission/boss progression.
3. Run the game in a browser, exercise controls and mission flow, capture a recent JPEG screenshot, and report completed scope and limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing Three.js gameplay and recent character, villain, collectible, and riddle changes.
- `index.html`: Game title/branding, HUD elements, start screen, and control hints.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no build or browser tests have been run.
- Existing game already had basic third-person movement, combat, character swapping, stealth, grapple/glide, vehicles, dialogue, a short campaign, and villain replay mode.

# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

## Objective
- Complete and validate the existing Three.js prototype for **BATMAN: SHADOWS OF GOTHAM**, a playable Batman and Robin action-adventure.

## Requirements
- Preserve character constraints: Robin has no cowl or detective mode; Alfred is not a superhero; distinguish villain appearances.
- Include 25 trophies, 15 clues, and 10 interactive riddles.
- Build and test without clarifying questions; state assumptions and limitations when finished.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing Three.js browser game.
- Scope the challenge count to 50 total: 25 trophies, 15 clues, and 10 riddles.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated branding, start screen, HUD, controls hint, character designs, villain dialogue and roster including Jason Todd.
- Added challenge collectibles, riddles, Batman-only detective vision, combo feedback, vehicle interactions, and story/boss progression.
- Added CSS for combo, detective vision, and riddle interfaces.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser startup and introductory dialogue tested; Batman detective vision activates while Robin is denied access as intended.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/gotham-in-game.jpg`.

### Active
- Test remaining gameplay and progression: combat, vehicle exit, collectibles, riddles, and boss sequence.
- Review for gameplay/UI issues and check browser console.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing of core controls and progression, including vehicle exit, collectibles, riddles, and boss fights.
2. Check for console issues beyond the observed missing favicon and WebGL performance warnings.
3. Summarize implementation, testing, assumptions, and prototype limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, characters, enemies, collectibles, riddles, controls, and story progression.
- `index.html`: Title, HUD, controls, start screen, and interaction UI.
- `style.css`: Game styling and HUD/riddle presentation.
- `/tmp/opencode/gotham-in-game.jpg`: Captured in-game screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes to `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- A short movement/attack input did not advance the objective or display a combo, so combat remains unverified.
- Browser console showed missing `favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL GPU stall warnings; no game-code runtime error was observed.
- This is a prototype, not a full-length realistic open-world game.
